# IOC Extractor 0.3.0

This release turns SQLite-backed IOC data into lifecycle-managed canonical
truth and adds controlled local/SMB import of structured CSV deliveries. It is
intended for operators who need fast event-driven intake and export without
sacrificing restart recovery, deterministic identity or bounded resource use.

## Highlights

- Fixed canonical record validity with active-only reads, typed history,
  bounded reconciliation and atomic mutable projection recovery.
- Stable sparse reusable export slots for immutable slices without renumbering
  surviving records.
- Contract-driven managed CSV import from local directories and SMB shares,
  including `as-is` and ordinary-pipeline `processed` modes.
- One-transaction cross-artifact import promotion with active-only patch
  semantics, declarative merge authority and exact crash-recovery receipts.
- A standalone `IOC_aggregate_generated.csv` projection and immutable export profile for
  IPv4, URL, FQDN and hash indicators with deterministic source-name updates.
- Event hints for low latency with durable ledgers and periodic reconciliation
  retained as the correctness path.

## Added

- `ioc.dataframe-import` source, authority, contract and runtime configuration.
- `ioc import validate`, `ioc import status` and `ioc import replay` operator
  commands.
- Local atomic ownership and SMB server-side claim/materialization/disposition,
  with optional WatchService and SMB2 `CHANGE_NOTIFY` hints.
- Canonical identity aliases and set-based active match planning for simple and
  compound artifact records.
- Managed-import health, safe aggregate reports, terminal retention and
  packaged runtime directories.
- Declarative multi-type column gates, ordered mutable-field policies and
  file/JDBC observation journals shared by document, oneshot and managed-import
  admission.

## Changed

- Dataframe SQLite schema advances through managed identity, sparse-slot and
  import-receipt migrations; service SQLite schema adds the managed delivery
  ledger and transition audit.
- The fresh production template uses fixed 12-hour validity and low-latency
  event-first cadences. Upgrade configuration remains explicit and fail-closed.
- Immutable export IDs are profile/artifact-scoped slots. Canonical row and
  lifecycle IDs remain internal and are never reused.
- `address_blacklist` and `hashes` use compound record identity while retaining
  their existing public CSV shapes.
- SMB endpoint encryption is now a closed `required|preferred|disabled` policy.
  The secure default permits only SMB3 and fails before share I/O unless
  effective session encryption is negotiated.
- Dataframe and service schemas advance to v11. A dataframe-owned monotonic
  observation order makes later registered nonempty aggregate names win even
  when processing completes out of order; retry and restart retain the order.

## Fixed

- Lifecycle deadline, projection and history work is bounded and recoverable
  after lost hints or restart.
- Revision-significant lifecycles create a new delivery even when reusable slots
  make bytes equal to an older slice.
- Managed import prevents partial branch writes, historical-row matches,
  per-row canonical transactions and retry overtaking.
- SMB import detects ownership collisions and source mutation without
  overwriting producer or private processing objects.
- Concurrent lifecycle/projection writers share one admission boundary;
  diagnostic delivery is bounded under duplicate-heavy input; managed import
  recognizes the public `NULL` token before value transforms.

## Upgrade notes

1. Stop the service and back up the complete `var/db` directory, configuration,
   environment file, export state and mutable projections.
2. Deploy 0.3.0 with managed import disabled. Validate the migrated service and
   dataframe databases and reconcile the new production template.
3. Activate fixed lifecycle for an existing dataframe database only through the
   documented two-restart `existing-records: expire` procedure. This one-way
   cutover deliberately expires legacy active rows.
4. Define and preview every import source/authority/contract before enabling
   managed intake. Import requires `lifecycle.validity.mode: fixed`.
5. The aggregate starts empty. Existing canonical rows are not backfilled into
   it; only newly accepted document, oneshot or explicitly configured managed
   aggregate-import observations populate the artifact.

Rollback: package activation can restore the previous release, its systemd unit
and the database backup while preserving operator configuration. After one-way
lifecycle activation or accepted 0.3.0 writes, restore the complete matching
rollback point; do not point older code at the upgraded live databases.

## Breaking or observable contract changes

- Fixed lifecycle changes active membership over time and adds a one-way
  activation boundary for existing databases.
- Immutable export `id` is now a stable reusable slot scoped by profile and
  artifact, not canonical storage identity.
- ECS structured fields use the current nested Spring Boot representation;
  consumers of older dotted keys must update their queries.
- Strict configuration rejects unknown and legacy `ioc.*` keys on YAML,
  environment, system-property and CLI channels.
- Legacy `ioc.sync.endpoints[].smb.encrypt` is temporarily accepted as a
  rollback bridge: `true` maps to `encryption: required`, `false` to `disabled`,
  and startup emits a value-free warning. New configurations must use the
  closed selector; setting both keys is rejected.
- SMB endpoints accept an optional `port` in the TCP range `1..65535`; omitting
  it preserves standard TCP/445 for regular, managed-import and
  `CHANGE_NOTIFY` sessions.
- `ioc_aggregate` has the exact public column order
  `name;ip_address;url_match;host_match;hash`. One initial row carries exactly
  one IOC value; multi-carrier correlation remains outside the 0.3.0 contract.
- A v11 database is not readable by the previous v9 binary. Rollback requires
  the matching pre-upgrade binary, configuration, both SQLite databases and
  service-owned files from one coordinated backup point.

## Known issues

- `ING-11`: ordinary daemon retry and run-ledger resume still require the
  dedicated lifecycle-hardening slice; current behavior is data-safe but may
  require operator attention after specific retry failures.
- `ING-13`: the full pre-claim source fate contract remains open.
- `OPS-8`: managed-import SMB contract qualification currently covers Samba;
  each explicitly supported Windows Server/NAS family needs the same live suite.

## Verification

- Full Maven reactor, architecture boundaries, quality analyzers, golden E2E,
  documentation links, managed-import smoke, lifecycle smoke and reference load
  are release gates.
- Packaged fresh-install, upgrade/rollback and live local/Samba qualification
  evidence is recorded against the final candidate commit; unavailable external
  server families are recorded as skips, never passes.
- SMB support under `encryption: required` needs the opt-in live encryption
  contract; earlier file-operation evidence without the effective policy is not
  treated as encryption proof.
- Local deployment rollback restores the version-matched systemd unit and the
  SQLite backup with its POSIX ACLs and extended attributes.
- Aggregate qualification covers fresh and upgraded databases, file and JDBC
  daemon ledgers, managed import success/quarantine, coordinated rollback and a
  duplicate-heavy 100,000/250,000-row load profile. The final 100,000-row
  candidate completed in 14.067 s with 599,724 KiB peak RSS and 5,067 aggregate
  rows; the 250,000-row candidate used 720,876 KiB peak RSS.
